annotation.title_clean: Establishing the Digital Europe programme for the period 2021-2027 — Amendments adopted by the European Parliament on 13 December 2018 on the proposal for a regulation (COM(2018)0434 — C8-0256/2018 — 2018/0227(COD))
annotation.title_en: Establishing the Digital Europe programme for the period 2021-2027 — Amendments adopted by the European Parliament on 13 December 2018 on the proposal for a regulation
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union C 388/775 (13.11.2020)
named_instruments_referenced: Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU
Communication on Artificial Intelligence for Europe COM(2018)237
annotation.summary_en: This document contains the European Parliament's first-reading amendments of 13 December 2018 to the proposed regulation setting up the Digital Europe Programme for 2021–2027. The programme funds high-performance computing, AI, cybersecurity, digital skills and the wider deployment of digital technology. The amendments add privacy-by-design and ethics-review conditions to AI funding and extend the AI objective to robotics powered by AI.
key_provisions_or_claims: Sets five specific objectives: high-performance computing; AI (and distributed ledgers); cybersecurity; advanced digital skills; and deployment and interoperability. The budget is about EUR 9.2 billion.
AI objectives should cover AI-powered robotics because European industry's demand for it is growing (recital 19c).
AI actions must comply with ethical principles and the Charter of Fundamental Rights. Each project gets an ethics review, and actions that are not ethically acceptable cannot receive funding.
AI solutions must respect privacy and security by design, and humans must remain at the centre of AI development and deployment.
Sets up a network of European Digital Innovation Hubs, with at least one per Member State, to help businesses, especially SMEs, adopt digital technology.
